content: The following is a guide to creating a WikiDoc landmark trial page. A landmark trial page is a comprehensive collection of all relevant information about a specific clinical study, including a detailed breakdown of its design, interventions, outcomes, randomization, statistical methods, limitations, and more. These pages are designed to allow users to efficiently access the content they are seeking, facilitate navigation of the study of interest, and ensure completeness and consistency across WikiDoc pages. Templates with standardized language are provided to assist in creating and editing these pages. Complete Title of Study This section should include the full name of the study in the first sentence. It should not include the study acronym. For example, the complete title of the RALES study was The effect of spironolactone on morbidity and mortality in patients with severe heart failure. Study Acronym This section should include the study acronym, which may not necessarily be derived from the initials of the study title. For example, RALES stands for Randomized Aldactone Evaluation Study for congestive heart failure. Principal Investigator, Co-investigators, and Collaborating Institutions This section should list the principal investigator, co-investigators, and collaborating institutions involved in the study. It should not include funding sources. Overview This section provides a general overview of the trial, including the study acronym in the first sentence. It serves as a summary of all the overview statements below it. Disease State(s) Studied This section should list all the major diseases studied in the trial, including both primary and secondary outcome diseases. Study Design This section should describe the study setting (e.g., multicenter or single-center, with the number of sites and countries if available), the type of blinding (e.g., single-blind, double-blind, open-label), the design (e.g., parallel arms, crossover, factorial, delayed-start), and the sample size (total number of randomized patients). This information can typically be found in the CONSORT flowchart, abstract, or study methods section. Study Duration and Time-points This section should include the total study duration, participant enrollment period, study start date, follow-up duration, and study visits (time-points where primary outcomes are assessed). It is also important to include stoppage criteria and reasons, if available. Interventions This section should describe all treatment arms studied in the trial, including both active comparator and experimental arms. Study Measures This section should detail the study measures used in the trial. Measures refer to the items in a research study to which participants respond. For example, if the outcome measure is cholesterol levels, it should specify how it is measured (e.g., milligrams per deciliter of blood) and how often it is assessed. Primary Endpoint This section describes the primary endpoint of the clinical trial, which is the main reason for randomizing subjects and powering the trial. The primary endpoint may include composite outcomes but should not include any statistical report. Secondary Endpoints This section describes the secondary endpoints of the clinical trial, which are analyzed post hoc and may not be powered or randomized. It is important to include all secondary endpoints but avoid including statistical reports. Inclusion Criteria This section outlines the characteristics that prospective subjects must have to be included in the study. Exclusion Criteria This section outlines the characteristics that disqualify subjects from being included in the study. Outcome: Primary Endpoint This section should describe the primary endpoint outcome results, comparing experimental and control arms. It should include the statistical report (e.g., relative risk, hazard ratio, odds ratio, standardized mean difference, p-value, number needed to treat). Outcome: Secondary Endpoint This section should describe the secondary endpoint outcome results, comparing experimental and control arms. It should include the statistical report. Outcome: Exploratory Endpoints This section should describe the exploratory endpoint outcome results, comparing experimental and control arms. It should include the statistical report. Subgroup Analysis This section should describe the subgroup analysis, comparing experimental and control arms. It should include the statistical report. Outcome: Safety Endpoints This section should describe the safety endpoint outcome results, comparing experimental and control arms. It should include the statistical report. Statistical Methods This section describes the statistical methods used in the clinical trial, including sample size calculation (if available), statistical tests used, descriptive statistics, power, and effect size. Conclusions This section summarizes the conclusions of the clinical trial. For example, it may state whether the active intervention is superior, inferior, or shows no difference compared to the control intervention in reducing or increasing the primary outcome. Discussion and Limitations of the Trial This section discusses the limitations of the trial, addressing potential sources of bias, imprecision, and, if relevant, the multiplicity of analyses. Commentary This section allows for personal comments about the study. Slides Attach PowerPoint slides corresponding to the trial. These can be downloaded from the WikiDoc journal club. Video Commentary Attach a YouTube video (if available) with study commentary and discussion.
